environment.prior_reproduction: The defect (persisted trusted project hook skipped by noninteractive codex exec unless --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust was supplied) was last reproduced by the issue owner on Codex CLI 0.144.4 on 2026-07-14. This witness reruns the identical paired arms on 0.144.5.

method.hook_instrument: A PATH-prepended fak.cmd shim intercepted the trusted hook command ('fak sessions codex-loop-hook'), logged each invocation, emitted {"decision":"block","reason":"fak 3939 witness sentinel"}, and exited 0. The trusted <repo-root>/.codex/hooks.json was never modified, so hooks/list kept reporting the same key and hash throughout.
method.traffic_discriminator: Each arm uses a deliberately invalid model slug (definitely-invalid-model-3939). If the hook is skipped the request reaches provider validation and fails HTTP 400 invalid_request_error; if the trusted blocking hook dispatches, the turn completes with all-zero token usage and no provider event.
method.privacy: Absolute paths are normalized to <repo-root>/<codex-home>. The fixed synthetic prompt is omitted. Thread ids are the same public witness handles the issue thread uses.
method.note: Every arm (including blocked ones) emits a local 'Model metadata for `definitely-invalid-model-3939` not found' item before turn.started; that is local metadata lookup, not provider traffic.

verdict: PROVEN on Codex CLI 0.144.5: noninteractive codex exec now honors persisted project-hook trust. A hook reported trusted by hooks/list dispatches without --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust from both the repository root and a nested cwd, and a blocking UserPromptSubmit decision stops the turn before any provider/model/tool traffic. The defect reported in issue #3939 (reproduced through 0.144.4) is no longer reproducible; the fix landed upstream in the Codex CLI, not in this repository.
